scenes.title: Demand
scenes.learning_objective: Reproduce the definition of demand and the law of demand.
scenes.narration: Demand is how much of a product buyers want at each price. The law of demand says that when the price rises, the quantity demanded falls. On a graph the demand curve slopes downward.
scenes.key_fact: The law of demand says that when the price rises, the quantity demanded falls.

scenes.title: Supply
scenes.learning_objective: Reproduce the definition of supply and the law of supply.
scenes.narration: Supply is how much sellers are willing to offer at each price. The law of supply says that when the price rises, sellers offer more. The supply curve slopes upward.
scenes.key_fact: The law of supply says that when the price rises, sellers offer more.

elements.description: Supply is how much sellers are willing to offer at each price.
The law of supply says that when the price rises, sellers offer more.

scenes.title: Equilibrium
scenes.learning_objective: Reproduce the definition of equilibrium and how it is determined.
scenes.narration: The equilibrium price is where the two curves cross: the amount buyers want equals the amount sellers offer. If the price is above it there is a surplus and prices tend to fall; below it there is a shortage and prices tend to rise. Example: if demand is Qd = 100 - 2P and supply is Qs = 20 + 2P, they are equal when 100 - 2P = 20 + 2P, so P = 20 and Q = 60.
